title: Galle Fort
summary: Galle Fort on the southwest coast of Sri Lanka began as a small Portuguese fortress, Santa Cruz, built in 1588. The Central Cultural Fund says the Dutch captured Galle in 1640 and built the surviving fortification system, with fourteen bastions, between 1663 and 1729. The Encyclopedia.com account of the Dutch East India Company dates the capture to 1640 temporarily and 1644 finally.

as_recorded.value: The Portuguese first built a small fortress at Galle in 1588

reviewer_note: The capture year differs: the CCF says the Dutch captured Galle in 1640, while Encyclopedia.com has 1640 as temporary and 1644 as final; both are stated. The Rijksmuseum label supports only that Galle was among the VOC's most important towns in Sri Lanka. A CCF page gives walls up to 12 m high and 10 m wide with fourteen bastions, but no UNESCO or scholarly page was opened, so no model block is written.
